method: All candidates and balanced weights retained; formulations, supports, route costs, order size, price annotations and rubric scores fixed. Monthly: 14 observed metal prices. Daily: 10 observed metal prices; all remaining prices at the 2026-08 reference. Exact date intersection; no interpolation. Prices vary, but not output, activity, durability or process revenue. Historical replay of the current model, not a historical recommendation backtest or observed industrial catalyst prices.
score_controls: Application: rounded score and cost tie-break; frozen rounded: nonprice scores fixed; continuous: additionally remove economics and total score rounding; fixed scale: additionally use the reference-month min/max without clipping. Evidence scores in the application depend on material cost shares. Reference-scale scores are diagnostic and can leave 0–100.

tolerances.materiality: 1% of the cheaper modeled cost is a descriptive screen, not an uncertainty bound

cr-doped-amorphous.title: Cr-doped amorphous NiFe route
decision_notes: Good fit when alkaline durability matters more than the lowest route complexity.
Chromium-doping and amorphous-state control raise route overhead relative to the simpler NiFe cases.

nife-seed-assisted.title: Seed-assisted NiFe anode
decision_notes: Use this when higher anode efficiency is worth tighter deposition control.
The route improves performance but gives up some simplicity relative to the plain NiFe-LDH baseline.

nico2o4-spinel.title: NiCo2O4 spinel anode
decision_notes: Adds the cobalt raw-material axis to a family that is otherwise all NiFe - the screen now prices Fe-vs-Co sensitivity directly.
Rides the family's co-precipitation/calcination route.

nife-ldh-scalable.title: NiFe-LDH scalable anode
decision_notes: Best starting point when the goal is a non-noble alkaline-electrolyzer anode with a credible scale-up story.
Economics stay favorable because the active phase avoids PGMs and the stack defaults use alkaline materials rather than PEM inputs.

co-mgo-la2o3.title: Co/MgO-La2O3 mid-cost route
decision_notes: The primary study supports 5 wt% Co and identifies Mg/La = 5 on a molar basis as its most active support; the retained 85 wt% MgO and 10 wt% La2O3 are not that formulation.
The review-derived 92% conversion was not reverified against the primary results and is not assigned to this proxy. Co/alumina spinel observations are not direct evidence for this Mg-La support.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

ni-mgo-ceo2-interface.title: Ni-MgO/CeO2 interface
decision_notes: The 15/15/70 wt% Ni/CeO2/MgO composition, 475-650 C window and generic oxide route are assumptions, not a reproduced literature recipe.
The primary paper uses 10 wt% Ni, CeO2:CNT = 0.5 by mass, NaBH4-assisted reduction and light; its activity cannot be transferred directly to this thermal MgO formulation.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

ni-alumina-baseline.title: Ni/gamma-Al2O3 baseline
decision_notes: The 12/88 wt% Ni/alumina composition and 550-700 C window are engineering screening assumptions; no exact primary recipe was verified.
Ni/Pt(111) simulations and carbon-supported CoMoFeNiCu alloys do not validate this monometallic gamma-alumina baseline. Support grade and precursor markup remain price proxies.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

ru-mgo-premium.title: Ru/MgO premium
decision_notes: The retained 3 wt% Ru cost input approximates a paper reporting 3.1 wt% Ru on preferential MgO(111) nanosheets, not commodity MgO of unspecified facet distribution.

The primary route includes special MgO preparation and Ru3(CO)12 deposition. The chloride-price anchor and generic impregnation route do not reproduce those procurement and manufacturing requirements.
GaN-supported Ru uses concentrated light and is not direct evidence for thermal Ru/MgO activity. The 400-575 C screening window is not a cross-study performance normalization.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

cs-co3mo3n.title: Cs-promoted Co3Mo3N nitride
decision_notes: The only non-Fe, non-Ru chemistry in the family; molybdenum inventory dominates the material term.
The 3x-Fe rate figure comes from literature excerpts quoting the primary papers, not from an abstract read directly - treat as indicative.

fused-iron-baseline.title: Promoted fused-iron (magnetite/wustite) baseline
decision_notes: Cheapest active metal in the family and a fully de-risked manufacturing chain; the cost of ownership sits in compression duty, not the catalyst.
Wustite variants trade the same formulation for ~70% higher activity, so the screen's iron term is conservative.

ru-graphite-kaap.title: Cs/Ba-promoted Ru on graphitized carbon (KAAP-type)
decision_notes: Commercially proven since the 1990s; choose it when milder loop pressure is worth the Ru inventory.
Promoter loadings are not disclosed in the open literature, so the Cs-Ba package weight is a screening assumption priced at cesium parity (conservative, barium is far cheaper).

ru-cafh-lowtemp.title: Ru/CaFH low-temperature architecture
decision_notes: Family performance ceiling for low-temperature operation; screen it to bound what the emerging class could cost, not as a procurement option.
Support economics are the dominant unknown: CaH2-grade hydride chemistry has no public bulk market.

cuo-ceo2.title: CuO-CeO2 (base-metal option)
decision_notes: The cost play: both oxides carry public prices and the combustion route is fast; accepts a narrower optimal window than nanogold below 100 C.
CuO screened at 7 wt%: the optimization exists in the cited full texts, the exact optimum was not abstract-verified.

pt-fe-alumina.title: Fe-promoted Pt/Al2O3 (fuel-processor standard)
decision_notes: The de-risked choice with the deepest kinetics record; platinum inventory is the cost driver at sub-percent loadings.
Fe promoter screened at 0.5 wt%: the promotion effect is source-quoted, its exact loading is not.

au-tio2-nanogold.title: Au/TiO2 nanogold (low-temperature)
decision_notes: Wins when the reformate train needs sub-100-C operation; loses on manufacturing tolerance (size control) and long-term carbonate deactivation.
Au loading screened at 2 wt%: class-typical (1-5 wt%), not stated in the fetched abstracts.

ag-co-mea.title: Ag CO-selective MEA cathode
decision_notes: The demonstrated-durability CO option: silver at roughly one-eightieth of gold's price with six-month continuous operation on record.
The Sustainion membrane term is part of the electrode stack, priced by the calculator's membrane row rather than this component list.

cu-multicarbon-co2rr.title: Cu multicarbon CO2RR cathode
decision_notes: Best fit when the program goal is multicarbon CO2 reduction (ethylene / ethanol) and a Cu cathode is acceptable.
Selectivity to C2 products improves with morphology control, but route maturity is lower than Au or Sn alternatives.

sn-formate-co2rr.title: Sn formate CO2RR cathode
decision_notes: Use this when liquid formate is the target product and a non-noble cathode in an alkaline / AEM stack is acceptable.
Cathode economics stay favorable because Sn avoids PGM exposure, but stack durability under formate flow remains a sensitivity.

au-co-co2rr.title: Au CO-selective CO2RR cathode
decision_notes: Use when high CO Faradaic efficiency is the program target and a precious-metal cathode is acceptable.
Catalyst economics are dominated by gold price exposure even at moderate loadings.

ni-ceo2-lowtemp.title: Ni/CeO2 low-temperature route
decision_notes: Same impregnation chain as the alumina baseline with the support upgraded to a public-priced reducible oxide.
Wins low-temperature duty without paying for ruthenium; ceria supply risk is the watch item.

ni-alumina-baseline.title: Ni/Al2O3 baseline
decision_notes: Best fit when a defensible non-noble commercial screening anchor matters more than the lowest possible light-off temperature.
Nickel still dominates the economic case even when advanced literature routes outperform it per active site.

ru-layered-titanate.title: Ru/layered titanate route
decision_notes: Strong candidate when the design target is ambient-pressure or much lower-temperature methanation rather than lowest catalyst cost.
Layered titanate confinement improves the performance score but keeps route reproducibility below industrial nickel practice.

ru-mnox-photothermal.title: Ru/MnOx photothermal route
decision_notes: Useful when lower reaction temperature or solar-assist compatibility matters enough to justify a noble-metal premium.
Photothermal and manganese-oxide route discipline reduce the maturity score versus the nickel baseline.

cza-baseline.title: Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 baseline
decision_notes: Best anchor for practical methanol screening because copper exposure stays visible and the route maps well onto established oxide-catalyst manufacturing.
Performance is not the family leader, but route maturity and reproducibility are the strongest.

cu-zrox-interface.title: Cu/ZrOx-MgO interface route
decision_notes: Useful when Cu economics still matter but the baseline CZA route leaves too much performance on the table.
Route overhead is higher because zirconia/basic-support contact and interface stability need tighter control.
The cited Cu/ZrOx-MgO study uses liquid-phase ALD. Its 14/21/65 wt% representation and generic processing chain are unvalidated screening proxies; ALD-specific processing cost is not estimated.

in2o3-zro2-lowtemp.title: In2O3-ZrO2 low-temperature route
decision_notes: Best fit when methanol selectivity at lower temperature is worth paying for a scarcer oxide system.
Indium inventory and oxide-state control keep this route less mature than Cu-led baselines.
Cited Ni/Pd-promoted and flame-made oxide systems provide architectural context. They do not validate this 55 wt% elemental-In/45 wt% ZrO2 recipe, temperature window, or assigned performance score.

pd-in2o3.title: Pd/In2O3 promoted oxide
decision_notes: The performance ceiling of the oxide branch; indium inventory, not palladium, dominates the material term.
Co-precipitation is source-supported; the reused Cu-Zn-Al processing chain and its labels are a costing proxy, not the reported Pd/In2O3 recipe.

families.title: CO2 hydrogenation to formate / formic acid reference family

pdag-ndcarbon-co2fa.title: PdAg / N-doped carbon
decision_notes: Best fit when a heterogeneous, separable catalyst is required and a small Pd / Ag inventory is acceptable.
N-doped carbon support supplies amine-style sites that stabilise CO2 / formate intermediates.

ru-sa-ldh.title: Single-atom Ru on Mg-Al LDH
decision_notes: Closes the solid-catalyst gap next to two pincer complexes and a PdAg alloy; separation economics favor it over homogeneous routes.
Ru loading screened at 0.5 wt%: single-site loadings are low by construction and the abstract states no weight figure.

ru-pincer-co2fa.title: Ru-pincer (Sanford / Beller-style)
decision_notes: Use when Ru chemistry is acceptable and cost reduction over Ir is desirable.
Pincer-ligand cost dominates total cost more than Ir route since Ru is cheaper per oz.

ir-pincer-co2fa.title: Ir-pincer (Tanaka / Nozaki anchor)
decision_notes: Best fit when very high turnover frequency is the program goal and Ir economics are acceptable.
Iridium price exposure dominates the cost basis; ligand-only proxy understates total catalyst cost.

ni-co-almgo.title: Ni-Co/Al-Mg-O bimetallic
decision_notes: The scalable coking answer beside single-site, zeolite-confined and iridium strategies.
Metal terms screened at the stability-optimized loadings (~4 wt% Ni, ~5.5 wt% Co on a mass basis from the reported molar loadings).

ni-single-atom-ceria.title: Ni/CeO2 single-site route
decision_notes: Strong non-noble DRM route when catalyst replacement and carbon management both matter.
Single-site or highly dispersed preparation keeps route maturity below simpler Ni-supported baselines.

ni-zeolite-stable.title: Ni-zeolite stabilized route
decision_notes: Best fit when you want a more transferable non-noble DRM route than single-site Ni while still improving stability.
Support engineering is the main route premium rather than raw-metal exposure.

ir-ceria-premium.title: Ir@CeO2-x premium
decision_notes: Performance leader for this family, but noble-metal exposure is hard to justify unless coking limits dominate economics.
Use as a premium benchmark rather than a default procurement basis.

agcs-industrial.title: Ag-Cs / Al2O3 (industrial standard)
decision_notes: Best fit for high-selectivity industrial duty without paying for Re-promotion overhead.
Catalyst economics dominated by Ag; Cs is a small fraction of cost but widens the selectivity window meaningfully.

ag-alumina-baseline.title: Ag / alpha-Al2O3 baseline
decision_notes: Most transferable ethylene-epoxidation basis with mature commercial inputs.
Without a promoter, EO selectivity is meaningfully lower than industrial Cs- or Cs/Re-promoted catalysts.

cu-ag-bimetallic.title: Cu-Ag/alpha-Al2O3 (DFT-designed alloy)
decision_notes: The only non-pure-silver chemistry beside three Ag/Al2O3 generations; the copper add costs essentially nothing against the silver inventory.
Modern commercial multi-promoter recipes live in patents; this is the best peer-reviewed alloy archetype.

agcsre-modern.title: Ag-Cs-Re / Al2O3 (modern HSE)
decision_notes: Best fit for the highest-selectivity industrial duty when Re-promoter overhead is acceptable.
Re exposure is small but Re prices are high; promoter precursor accounting dominates non-Ag cost.

fe-silica-lower-olefin.title: Fe / SiO2 lower-olefin FT
decision_notes: Best fit when the program target is lower olefins (C2=-C4=) rather than heavier paraffins.
Iron is far cheaper than cobalt but methane selectivity is higher; promoter (K, Mn) discipline matters.

fe-cu-k-precipitated.title: Precipitated Fe-Cu-K (Sasol-class)
decision_notes: The bulk-iron economics anchor beside two supported-cobalt systems and a model iron catalyst.
Promoter levels follow Bukur's parts-per-100-Fe convention translated to a mass basis for the screen.

co-alumina-fts.title: Co / Al2O3 FT (commercial baseline)
decision_notes: Most transferable FT basis and the clearest commercial comparison point for low-temperature GTL.
Catalyst economics dominated by Co loading and Re / Pt promoter; alumina support is a small fraction of cost.

co-cnt-structured.title: Co / CNT structured FT
decision_notes: Use this when CNT-support architecture is acceptable and tighter Co dispersion control is desired.
Catalyst economics shift toward CNT support cost; active-Co reducibility window is wider than alumina-supported.

co-nc-nonnoble.title: Co-SAs/NPs@NC route
decision_notes: Useful when the program goal is to avoid palladium while keeping hydrogen-release performance credible.
Pyrolysis and acid-wash complexity reduce reproducibility versus the supported-Pd baseline.

ptmo-gasphase-premium.title: Pt-Mo ensemble route
decision_notes: Best used when gas-phase formic-acid dehydrogenation and very low CO are worth a platinum premium.
Pt and Mo ensemble control improves the performance score but keeps the route less mature than supported Pd.

pd-carbon-baseline.title: Pd/C baseline
decision_notes: Best fit when a familiar and defensible supported-Pd screening anchor is needed for LOHC hydrogen-release work.
Palladium keeps route maturity high, but catalyst economics remain exposed to precious-metal pricing.

aupd-mil101.title: Au-Pd in amine-grafted MIL-101
decision_notes: Adds the Au-bimetallic + functionalized-porous-support archetype next to Pd/C, single-atom Co and Pt-Mo.
Operating temperatures sit in the papers' bodies, not the abstracts; the window shown is the ambient-to-mild band the chemistry targets.

fen-c-pgmfree-cathode.title: Fe-N-C PGM-free cathode
decision_notes: The strongest noble-metal-avoidance route in this family, but durability and process reproducibility still lag Pt-based cathodes.
Economics are attractive because metal exposure is low, yet route complexity is dominated by pyrolysis and post-treatment control.

ptco-intermetallic-cathode.title: Pt-Co intermetallic cathode
decision_notes: Best fit when PEMFC cathode performance is worth extra alloying and transition-metal retention discipline.
Still expensive because Pt remains the dominant cost driver, but the route can justify higher utilization targets.

ptc-baseline-cathode.title: Pt/C baseline cathode
decision_notes: Most transferable PEMFC cathode basis and the clearest commercial comparison point.
Economics remain dominated by live Pt price exposure even when route maturity is high.

ptni-octahedra.title: PtNi octahedra (mass-activity ceiling)
decision_notes: Screens the upper bound of Pt-mass reduction between the Pt/C baseline, the PtCo intermetallic and the PGM-free entry.
Solvothermal shape control (W(CO)6-steered growth, surfactant stripping) is the readiness discount; the material bill itself is ordinary.

niooh-glycerol-anode.title: NiOOH non-noble glycerol anode
decision_notes: Best fit when avoiding PGMs is the program goal and dihydroxyacetone / glycolate selectivity is acceptable.
Selectivity is governed by NiOOH cycling; cell design must accommodate Ni3+ regeneration.

pt-c-glycerol-anode.title: Pt / C glycerol anode
decision_notes: Best fit when low onset potential matters more than full PGM avoidance.
Catalyst economics dominated by Pt loading even at 20 wt%.

pt-bi-dha.title: Pt-Bi DHA-selective anode
decision_notes: DHA sells far above generic oxidation products; this candidate screens the selectivity economics the other three cannot.
The bismuth modifier is irreversibly adsorbed onto commercial Pt/C, so the route is the family's standard chain plus a bath step.

au-c-glycerol-selectivity.title: Au / C glycerol anode (selectivity)
decision_notes: Best fit when the program target is selective C3 oxygenate production rather than total oxidation.
Au has a higher onset potential than Pt; trade overpotential for selectivity.

comos-hdo.title: CoMoS / Al2O3 sulfide HDO
decision_notes: Best fit when industrial hydrotreating-style HDO is acceptable and sulfided-catalyst handling is in scope.
Sulfidation discipline (atmosphere, temperature ramp) drives long-hold activity.

The cited surface-engineered CoMoS nanosulfide is not evidence for the retained 12/4/84 wt% Mo/Co/alumina composition. Sulfur inventory and the exact precursor/sulfidation recipe are not resolved by these elemental cost fractions.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

nimo-carbon-hdo.title: NiMo / carbon (acid-free)
decision_notes: The primary Ni1Mo3N/C uses a 1:3 Ni/Mo molar ratio, glucose-derived carbon and sol-gel preparation followed by 500 C H2 treatment. The retained 5/10/85 wt% Ni/Mo/activated-carbon recipe is not its measured composition.

The paper tests phenolics at 220-260 C; the retained 250-380 C window and generic impregnation route are screening assumptions. Do not transfer its activity to a simple sulfur-free NiMo alloy or to commodity activated carbon.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

pt-silica-hdo.title: Pt / SiO2 HDO
decision_notes: The 1 wt% Pt loading, silica grade, 250-400 C window and generic preparation route are engineering assumptions; the accessible primary abstract describes m-cresol at 300 C.
Pt-Sn monoliths, other oxide supports and isolated-Pt studies are contextual literature, not direct evidence for the screened unpromoted Pt/silica recipe.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

ru-carbon-hdo.title: Ru/C noble-metal route
decision_notes: The paper distinguishes Ru loading within the catalyst from catalyst intake relative to oil. The 65 wt% oil yield must not be paired with an unverified simultaneous 90 wt% deoxygenation claim.
Carbon grade, manufacturing details and the full 250-350 C screening window are not established by the accessible abstract; the shared generic carbon route remains a cost proxy.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

nimo-alkaline-her-cathode.title: NiMo alkaline HER cathode
decision_notes: Use this when avoiding PGMs is the program goal and an alkaline / AEM stack is acceptable.
Earth-abundant chemistry keeps catalyst economics low at the cost of slightly higher overpotential than Pt/C.

mos2-acidic-her-cathode.title: MoS2 acidic HER cathode
decision_notes: Use when an acidic non-noble HER cathode is desired and the program can absorb lower route maturity for catalyst-economics upside.
Long-term acidic stability and reproducible edge-site population remain the main risks versus the Pt/C anchor.

pt-carbon-her-cathode.title: Pt/C HER cathode (PEM)
decision_notes: Most transferable HER cathode basis and the clearest commercial comparison point for PEM electrolyzer stacks.
Economics remain dominated by live Pt price exposure even at low cathode loading.

ru-c2n-her.title: Ru@C2N pH-universal cathode
decision_notes: Prices the Ru-for-Pt substitution between the Pt/C baseline and the two non-PGM entries.
C2N is an engineering price proxy. The public supplementary methods identify hexaaminobenzene preparation; no source-matched melamine-to-C2N cost conversion or bulk C2N quotation was verified.

activated-carbon-autocatalytic.title: Activated-carbon consumable catalyst
decision_notes: Lowest catalyst cost and trivially manufacturable, but conversion (25-40%) and deactivation by pore blocking cap performance.
Continuous make-up consumption means the screen's per-pound price is closer to an operating cost than a one-time charge.

fe-alumina-pyrolysis.title: Fe/Al2O3 higher-temperature route
decision_notes: Preferred anchor when metal cost dominates: iron is the cheapest active metal in the family and 69% conversion at 700 C is documented.
Higher furnace duty than the Ni route is a process cost outside this catalyst screen.

ni-sio2-highload.title: High-loading Ni/SiO2
decision_notes: Best fit when moderate temperature and high hydrogen purity matter more than catalyst lifetime.
Economics hinge on nickel recovery from the spent carbon-metal composite; the screen prices fresh catalyst only.

molten-ni-bi.title: Molten Ni-Bi alloy media
decision_notes: The melt is a one-time inventory rather than a consumable, so the per-pound screen overstates its lifetime cost - noted, not modeled.
Bismuth dominates the material term at the 73 wt% melt fraction.

hzsm5-mth.title: H-ZSM-5 (MTH baseline)
decision_notes: Use when the program target includes aromatic gasoline-range or methanol-to-aromatics products rather than light olefins.
MFI pore geometry favors C5+ relative to chabazite, with stronger Bronsted acidity.

zn-zsm5-aromatics.title: Zn / ZSM-5 (aromatics-leaning)
decision_notes: Use when the program goal is BTX or aromatic gasoline rather than light olefins.
Adding the Zn pass improves aromatic selectivity but increases catalyst cost and adds a deactivation pathway.

sapo-34-light-olefin.title: SAPO-34 chabazite (DMTO baseline)
decision_notes: Most transferable MTO basis and the dominant commercial light-olefin route.
Deactivation through coke remains the main process-side cost driver; high-pressure H2 co-feed mitigates lifetime loss.

nano-sapo-34.title: Nanosized SAPO-34 (lifetime play)
decision_notes: Benchmarks what nano-morphology is worth against the standard SAPO-34: same material bill, longer life, harder synthesis.
Operating temperature/WHSV are not stated in the fetched abstracts; the window shown is the standard MTO band.

v2o5-wo3-tio2.title: V2O5-WO3/TiO2 monolith (stationary standard)
decision_notes: The retained 2.5 wt% V2O5, 7 wt% WO3 and 90.5 wt% TiO2 are screening inputs. The service study instead reports 3.51 wt% V2O5 and 6.36 wt% WO3, plus reinforcing fibers and other constituents.

The 260-420 C screening window is not the approximately 200 C service temperature in the 18,000 h case. Catalyst-grade anatase, forming aids, monolith geometry and price parity with TiO2 pigment remain assumptions.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

fe-zsm-5.title: Fe-ZSM-5 high-temperature variant
decision_notes: The Long-Yang primary abstract reports nearly complete NO conversion at 400-500 C and strong exchange-level and Si/Al effects; it does not establish the retained 2 wt% Fe recipe or 300-550 C window.

The Fe small-pore-zeolite review concerns other framework types and does not prove superior stability of this ZSM-5 candidate. Generic ion exchange, commodity support pricing and isolated-Fe speciation remain assumptions.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

cu-ssz-13.title: Cu-SSZ-13 (diesel aftertreatment standard)
decision_notes: The primary Cu-SSZ-13 study establishes the architecture and activity/selectivity relative to Cu-beta and Cu-ZSM-5, but the exact 2.5 wt% Cu recipe was not verified from accessible primary experimental text.

Cu loading, Si/Al ratio, hydrothermal-aging conditions, washcoat/substrate mass and the 200-500 C screening window must be specified for a quantitative comparison. The SSZ-13 material price remains an engineering proxy.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

plasma-nrr.title: Plasma-NRR ammonia route
decision_notes: Use when a non-electrochemical pathway is acceptable and plasma equipment is available.
Energy efficiency remains the main bottleneck; trap-side recovery design dominates cost.

li-mediated-nrr.title: Lithium-mediated NRR cathode
decision_notes: Best fit when rigorous, reproducible NH3 production matters more than aqueous simplicity.
Cost is dominated by THF / Li salt cycle and inert-atmosphere stack hardware rather than catalyst material.

aqueous-nrr-cu.title: Aqueous NRR research anchor (Cu)
decision_notes: Use this only as a screening anchor; ambient aqueous NRR claims have a high false-positive rate without 15N2 isotope verification.
If the program target is real NH3 production, prefer the lithium-mediated or plasma routes above.

li-flow-shuttle.title: Li-mediated flow cell with proton shuttle
li-flow-shuttle.composition: 100.0% Li-mediated GDE assembly (Li salt + phosphonium shuttle)
decision_notes: Upgrades the family's Li-mediated line from batch proof-of-concept to continuous flow with isotope-grade verification.
The Pt-Au hydrogen-oxidation anode and pressurized handling are stack costs outside this catalyst-charge screen.

wo3-silica-oct.title: WO3 / SiO2 (Lummus OCT)
decision_notes: The 7 wt% cost input is elemental W, not WO3 mass. Silica grade, the 300-450 C window and industrial manufacturing assumptions were not verified against a licensor recipe.
The Handzlik molybdena study does not validate this tungsten catalyst; retained reviews supply industrial and supported-oxide context only.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

mo-silica-alumina.title: MoO3 / SiO2-Al2O3 emerging
decision_notes: The Handzlik primary study directly examines Mo on silica-alumina using thermal spreading of MoO2(acac)2, not the screened generic wet route. The 8 wt% input is elemental Mo, not MoO3.

Merle studies grafted Mo species on silica rather than silica-alumina; the W alkane-metathesis paper is not direct evidence for this candidate. Exact support composition, loading and the 100-300 C screening window remain assumptions.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

w-h-alumina.title: W-H/Al2O3 single-site hydride
decision_notes: Screens the feed-simplification upside (no 2-butene loop) against a lab-bound air-free synthesis.
Operating conditions are not stated in the fetched abstract; the window shown is the mild band this chemistry targets. W loading screened at 4 wt%.

The title and primary bibliographic record support the tungsten-hydride/ethylene-to-propylene architecture. Free full experimental conditions and the 4 wt% W recipe were not verified; metal-price markup does not establish the cost of air-free organometallic precursor preparation.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

re2o7-alumina-mild.title: Re2O7 / Al2O3 mild-condition
decision_notes: Best fit when mild-condition metathesis is required and Re economics are acceptable.
Catalyst economics dominated by Re; Al2O3 support is a small fraction of cost.

The screened 8 wt% is elemental Re, not Re2O7 mass. The Balcar primary abstract reports an optimum 9-15 wt% Re on organized mesoporous alumina; loading, pore structure and the 25-100 C window are retained as proxy inputs.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

pem-low-ir-interface.title: Low-Ir interface-engineered PEM route
decision_notes: This is the strongest low-Ir screening route now that the family explicitly prices membrane, ionomer, and titanium-side hardware instead of only powder mass.
Route discipline is tighter than the baseline because low-Ir utilization depends on interfacial contact, reconstruction control, and narrow loading windows.

pem-ru-rich-acidic.title: Ru-rich acidic OER route
decision_notes: This is the current price-pressure relief route because RuO2 is materially cheaper than IrO2 in the library, and the benchmark now reflects that directly in electrode-layer costing.
Use it as a scenario route, not the default procurement basis, because acidic durability and impurity tolerance still lag the best Ir-focused PEMWE routes.

iro2-tio2-supported.title: IrO2/TiO2 supported anode
decision_notes: The middle path between the pure-IrO2 baseline and the exploratory low-Ir entries: proven dilution on a public-priced support.
Adams-fusion synthesis (molten NaNO3) rides the family's standard route with its markup carried on the iridium term.

pem-irox-baseline.title: IrO2 PEM anode baseline
decision_notes: Most defensible PEM electrolyzer starting point because every layer in the stack is anchored to public catalog data or top-journal route references.
Economics are still dominated by scarce Ir powder and titanium-side hardware, so this route is the right control case rather than the cost winner.

tio2-photo-co2.title: TiO2 photocatalyst (UV anchor)
decision_notes: Most transferable photocatalyst basis for CO2 reduction screening.
UV-only activity caps solar-to-product performance versus visible-light variants.

gcn-sns2-zscheme.title: g-C3N4 / SnS2 Z-scheme
decision_notes: Best fit when visible-light operation is required and metal-free polymer + sulfide stack is acceptable.
Heterojunction reproducibility and SnS2 stability under irradiation are the main route-maturity concerns.

bivo4-visible.title: Monoclinic BiVO4 (visible-light oxide)
decision_notes: The visible-light single-oxide option beside UV-only titania and two heterojunction builds.
Priced on the contained-metal floor of its two elements, both public-quoted.

cu2o-mof-co2.title: Cu2O / MOF heterojunction
decision_notes: Best fit when high CO2 adsorption capacity is the program target.
MOF cost and Cu2O surface stability under photocatalysis remain the main risks.

pt-tio2-cocatalyst.title: Pt / TiO2 cocatalyst
decision_notes: Use when boosting H2 evolution rate is worth Pt exposure and a TiO2 base is acceptable.
Activity gains plateau at low Pt loading; further Pt addition adds cost without proportional activity.

tio2-anatase-baseline.title: TiO2 (anatase) baseline
decision_notes: Most transferable oxide photocatalyst basis and the clearest comparison anchor across the literature.
UV-only activity limits solar-to-hydrogen performance versus visible-light variants.

gcn-metal-free.title: g-C3N4 metal-free photocatalyst
decision_notes: Use when avoiding metals altogether is the program goal and visible-light operation is required.
Pyrolysis precursor choice and exfoliation discipline drive activity reproducibility.

srtio3-al-qe-benchmark.title: SrTiO3:Al with Rh/Cr2O3 + CoOOH
decision_notes: Screens what the QE ceiling costs: a rhodium term at one weight percent dominates an otherwise commodity oxide.
UV-only absorption is the documented limitation - efficiency, not solar coverage, is what this candidate benchmarks.

crox-alumina-catofin.title: CrOx/Al2O3 (Catofin-type)
decision_notes: The Pt-free industrial reference: pick it when metal inventory dominates the decision and cyclic operation is acceptable.
Chromium environmental-handling burden is a real cost outside this screen; noted, not priced.

bn-odhp.title: h-BN ODHP route
decision_notes: Use when an oxidative pathway is acceptable and a metal-free catalyst is the program goal.
Combustion / over-oxidation control becomes the main process risk versus the established Pt-Sn route.

ptsn-alumina-pdh.title: Pt-Sn / Al2O3 (Oleflex-style)
decision_notes: Most transferable PDH basis and the clearest commercial comparison point.
Catalyst economics dominated by Pt exposure even at low loadings; Sn promoter mitigates coking.

ptzn-intermetallic-pdh.title: PtZn intermetallic / zeolite
decision_notes: Best fit when long-hold stability and reduced regen cycles matter more than the Pt-Sn maturity.
Zeolite-encapsulation discipline reduces route confidence; intermetallic phase formation needs strict reduction temperature control.

cu-ceria-baseline.title: Cu/CeO2 baseline
decision_notes: Best fit when you want to stay on broadly traded metals and still push RWGS toward lower temperature.
Ceria handling adds some route overhead, but economics remain materially easier than Pt-led routes.

mo2n-hightemp.title: Mo2N high-temperature route
decision_notes: Best cost-pressure-relief route in this family when the reactor can tolerate a hotter operating window.
Nitride formation and deactivation control are the main route risks rather than raw-material cost.

cs-fe-cu-alumina.title: Cs-Fe-Cu/Al2O3 high-temperature route
decision_notes: The non-precious high-temperature workhorse beside the low/mid-temperature Cu, Pt and nitride entries.
Fe/Cu/Cs loadings are screening assumptions (15/3/1 wt%): the cited abstract establishes the formulation and ranking but states no weight loadings.

pt-tio2-premium.title: Pt/TiO2 premium
decision_notes: Performance leader for colder RWGS operation, but the economics are dominated by Pt exposure.
Most useful as a premium benchmark or when reactor thermal limits are tight.

nizn-intermetallic.title: NiZn intermetallic (non-Pd)
decision_notes: Removes the palladium term entirely; commercial maturity, not chemistry, is what holds the score down.
Ni/Zn loadings are screening assumptions (15/5 wt%): the cited abstracts establish the alloy strategy without weight loadings.

pdcu-saa.title: Pd-Cu single-atom alloy
decision_notes: Best fit when Pd intensity must be minimised and high ethylene selectivity is the program goal.
Sub-monolayer Pd reproducibility is the main route-maturity risk; SAA preparation discipline lowers route confidence vs Pd-Ag.

pd-alumina-baseline.title: Pd / Al2O3 baseline
decision_notes: Most transferable selective-hydrogenation basis with mature commercial inputs.
Without a promoter, the ethylene-selectivity window is narrow and over-hydrogenation risk is higher than Pd-Ag.

pdag-bimetallic.title: Pd-Ag bimetallic (front-end style)
decision_notes: Best fit for front-end ethylene-purification duty where the ethylene-selectivity window must stay wide.
Catalyst economics dominated by Pd; Ag is a small fraction by mass but widens the operability window meaningfully.

ni-calcium-aluminate.title: Ni on calcium aluminate (industrial baseline)
decision_notes: The reference economics for hydrogen at scale: cheap metal, fully de-risked manufacture, lifetime governed by sintering/carbon/sulfur rather than catalyst price.
Composition basis: 18-19 wt% NiO rows documented in the cited characterization studies; K linkage to naphtha duty is industrial practice not re-verified from a primary abstract.

sn-ni-coking-resistant.title: Sn/Ni surface alloy (coking-resistant)
decision_notes: The alloy-design answer to the baseline's carbon limit at nearly base-metal economics.
Sn and Ni loadings are screening assumptions (15 wt% Ni, 0.5 wt% Sn): the cited abstracts establish the trace-Sn surface-alloy strategy but do not state weight loadings.

rh-alumina-compact.title: Rh/Al2O3 compact-reformer route
decision_notes: Pick when compactness or membrane integration outweighs metal cost; the small order size reflects the niche duty.
Loading screened at 1 wt% Rh, inside the 0.5-2 wt% band the compact-reformer literature documents.

cza-industrial.title: Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 (industrial workhorse)
decision_notes: The reference economics of the family: cheap metals, the deepest industrial record in this database, and manufacturing quality riding on precipitation control.
Composition screened at the 60/30/10 CuO/ZnO/Al2O3 class figure quoted in the open-access review; Saito's best coprecipitate (51 wt% Cu, 22 wt% Zn metal basis) is consistent.

ga-promoted-cza.title: Ga-promoted Cu/ZnO (Zn-coverage engineering)
decision_notes: The incremental-upgrade play: same plant chain as the baseline, activity and stability bought with a few percent of promoter oxide.
Gallium is the expensive promoter choice; the same route carries ZrO2 promotion at commodity cost if the Ga term dominates the screen.

pd-zno-intermetallic.title: Pd/ZnO intermetallic alternative
decision_notes: Screen it to bound what RWGS suppression is worth: palladium restricts the route to niche duty against the copper baseline.
Performance evidence is from CO2-rich feeds; it supports the archetype but is not a pure-CO syngas benchmark.

cu-zno-baseline.title: Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 baseline
decision_notes: Best fit when the goal is a defensible industrial WGS screening anchor with transparent copper exposure.
Route maturity is highest in the family even if the absolute activity ceiling is lower than Pt-led routes.

co-ceria-interface.title: Co-CeO2 interface route
decision_notes: Strong option when non-noble pricing matters but a plain Cu/ZnO basis is too conservative on low-temperature performance.
The route premium comes from interfacial discipline and ceria handling rather than raw-metal scarcity.

fe-cr-hts.title: Fe2O3-Cr2O3(-CuO) high-temperature shift
decision_notes: The upstream stage of the industrial two-stage shift: cheapest metals in the family and a fully de-risked route, equilibrium-limited at its higher operating temperature.
Hexavalent-chromium handling during manufacture is a compliance cost outside this screen; noted, not priced.

pt-ceria-premium.title: Pt/CeO2 premium
decision_notes: Performance leader for colder WGS duty, but economics are directly tied to Pt exposure.
Use as a premium benchmark for hydrogen-polishing scenarios rather than a default cost anchor.
